title: Lemon-scented Gum: Ancient Lemon-scented Gums You Can Visit
meta_description: The Queensland gum whose leaf oil is sold as insect repellent. Melbourne's is 21 metres tall; Santa Barbara made five on its library grounds a landmark.
intro: Crush a leaf and the tree names itself. Lemon-scented gum carries so much citronellal in its foliage that the oil is distilled and sold as insect repellent. It comes from a modest patch of inland north Queensland, most botanists now file it under Corymbia rather than Eucalyptus, and it is planted around the warm half of the world for its smooth, pale, powdery trunk. In Madden Grove, on Melbourne parkland that has been public since 1862, the City of Yarra measured one in 2012 at 21 metres tall and 3.24 metres round and gave it 81 to 100 years. Santa Barbara has five on its public library grounds, about eighty years old in 2012 by the local paper's account, and made all five a landmark that October, in the same season as plans for the grounds that would have taken out three. In a Las Vegas county park, the Nevada Big Tree Register recorded one at 84 feet tall in 2015. Those figures are more than a decade old, and a July 2025 windstorm cost the valley many mature trees.
